title: Pulsed reserve allocator and customer-facing invoice allocation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: design and implement a Pulsed Reserve Allocator (PRA) that provides short-lived headroom for Dedicated tenants, ties usage to a clear invoice allocation model, and integrates with autoscaling policies and fleet controls.

Background: Customers on Dedicated capacity occasionally need transient headroom beyond their committed throughput — e.g., traffic spikes, feature launches, or load-testing windows. Existing surge mechanisms provision short buffers but: (a) attribution on invoices is opaque, (b) operator controls are coarse, and (c) autoscaling/throughput guarantees are not linked to the lifecycle of those transient boosts.

This ticket scopes the PRA core algorithm, the billing allocation model for temporary boosts (line-item and reconciliation semantics), the operator playbook (revoke/convert/pause), and the integration points with autoscaling controllers and tenant-facing console explanations. The design should prioritize predictable tenant-perceived latency, bounded cost exposure, and clear dispute pathways for invoices.

In-scope:
- Time-bounded reserve leases (pulses) with configurable TTLs and soft/hard caps.
- Allocation algorithm that charges pulses as prorated line-items with a clear amortization window.
- Hooks in the autoscaler so PRA pulses can trigger additional ephemeral workers or be satisfied by bursting into global surge pools.
- Operator controls: list active pulses, force-revoke, convert remaining pulse to overage (with audit trail).
- Console UX strings and an invoice preview API for customers when a pulse is requested.
- Metrics and traces: per-tenant pulse consumption, pulse-hit-rate, reconciliation deltas.

Out-of-scope: long-term reserved capacity (reserved fleets) redesign, wholesale billing model overhaul, or on-prem private network packaging (handled in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: PRA core service implemented with API: create_pulse, query_pulse, revoke_pulse, convert_pulse_to_overage
Pulse TTL enforcement and automatic expiry that returns unused portion to billing reconciler
Invoice allocation shows prorated pulse line-item and ties to tenant invoice rows (demoable on staging)
Autoscaler integration: pulse can request ephemeral workers and fallback to surge pool when global capacity is available
Operator UI: list and force-revoke pulses; actions are auditable with timestamp and operator id
Observability: dashboards for pulse adoption, cost delta, and reconciliation mismatch metrics >= 95% correctness in tests
E2E test simulating a 10x short spike with pulse acquisition, expiry, and invoice generation validated in CI
updates: 2026-02-11: Spike modelling done — we validated 3 realistic tenant spike shapes (fast-rise, plateau, trailing). Decided TTL defaults: 10m (short), 1h (medium), 6h (extended).
2026-02-13: Algorithm proposal added: time-decay credits with proportional amortization; small tenants get capped pulse size to avoid runaway costs. Shared with PM and FinOps.

2026-02-15: Prototype PRA API sketch completed. Implemented local in-memory allocator and smoke tests for TTL expiry. Integration plan with autoscaler drafted (controller hook points and backpressure signals).
2026-02-18: Billing team reviewed invoice line-item semantics — agreed on prorated per-minute line items and a reconciliation job that runs hourly to move unused pulse amounts to a credit bucket.

2026-02-16 - Lina Gomez (SRE): Autoscaler hook looks fine; be explicit about circuit-breaker signals to avoid thrashing when global surge pool is saturated.

owner_notes: Implementation plan: split into backend (allocator + billing hooks) and autoscale integration (controller adapter). Backend first — need prod-ready reconciliation before enabling UI previews.
Risk: high-frequency short pulses could increase reconciliation load. Add a batching window and rate-limit pulse creation per-tenant to mitigate.
Next steps: schedule a 30-minute sync with Billing and SRE (requested for 2026-02-22).
